editorial.meta_description: The Certified Records Manager exam evaluates professional expertise across six distinct domains to validate industry standards in records and information.
editorial.overview: The CRM Certified Records Manager certification, administered by the Institute of Certified Records Managers (ICRM), validates professional expertise in records and information management. The exam assesses knowledge across six distinct domains, ranging from management principles and information creation to technology and business cases. It ensures that professionals can effectively manage records throughout their entire lifecycle in compliance with established industry standards and various regulatory requirements necessary for organizational success and data integrity. This assessment process confirms that candidates possess the skills to maintain high-quality information governance within their respective organizations, covering the full scope of records management practices and professional responsibilities required for certification.
editorial.who_should_take: This certification is intended for records and information management professionals. Candidates should possess significant experience in managing records, implementing retention schedules, and overseeing complex information systems within their organizations to ensure ongoing compliance, data security, and operational efficiency across all departments.
editorial.preparation_strategy: Review the six domains outlined by the ICRM to understand the scope of the 502 questions. Focus on the core principles of records management, including retention, disposition, and the use of technology in information systems. Utilize official annotated outlines for each part to guide your study. Ensure you understand the regulatory environment and the role of the National Archives and Records Administration in records management to achieve the required 70% passing score. Consistent review of these materials is helpful for success.

domain_guidance.summary: This domain covers the management principles and the structure of a records and information management program, focusing on management functions, program implementation, and the strategic alignment of records management with broader organizational goals and objectives.

This domain addresses the creation and use of records, including information frameworks, risk assessments, compliance, and privacy protections, ensuring that all information is managed securely from its initial creation through its active use phase.

This domain focuses on the physical and digital storage of records, including retrieval processes, conversion methods, and facility management, ensuring that records are accessible, protected, and maintained in appropriate environments throughout their required retention periods.

This domain covers the identification, retention, protection, and final disposition of records, ensuring they are managed according to legal and regulatory requirements while maintaining the integrity of the records throughout their entire lifecycle.

This domain examines the role of technology in records management, including system development life cycles and information systems, focusing on how digital tools support the efficient management and long-term preservation of organizational records.

This domain focuses on the development and application of business cases within the context of records and information management programs, emphasizing the financial and operational justification required for implementing new records management initiatives.

editorial.exam_day_guidance: Arrive prepared to answer 502 questions. Manage your time effectively across the six domains to ensure all sections are completed. Ensure you are familiar with the regulatory definitions and standards provided in the official documentation to support your responses and achieve the 70% passing score.

faq.question_title: How many questions are on the exam?
faq.answer_text: The CRM Certified Records Manager exam consists of exactly 502 questions covering the six domains of records and information management, requiring candidates to demonstrate expertise across all areas of the field.

The passing score for the CRM Certified Records Manager exam is 70%. Candidates must achieve this threshold to successfully earn their certification and demonstrate their proficiency in records management standards.

The provided documentation does not specify the exact duration of the exam. Please check with the Institute of Certified Records Managers (ICRM) for specific timing details and scheduling information before your test date.

faq.question_title: What is the current certification path?
faq.answer_text: The CRM Certified Records Manager certification is current. For information regarding the certification path or any updates, check with the Institute of Certified Records Managers (ICRM) for the most accurate and official guidance.
